doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-04-02

title: First trip to New Orleans: Sadie's boat, Nighthawk Orchestra and Mac's band
summary: Billie describes coming from Birmingham's Nighthawk Orchestra to fill in for sick Sadie on a lake steamer, meeting Buddy Petit and Lawrence Toca, then joining Mac Merrimickle's band and Joe People's in Orlando.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: Well, you might tell some of the early bands you played with when you left the, the shows. When did you come to New Orleans, Billy?

Well, I came to New Orleans and, I made it, my first trip to New Orleans, that's when my sister Sadie were here. She was playing on Steamer Madison Boat. That's when her and, uh, her first husband was together. Bebe Chani. Oh, yeah. Drummer. Well, she taken sick, well, I was, I was playing with the Nighthawk Orchestra band in Birmingham. So, after she told me she was sick, I left Birmingham and came to New Orleans. That's when my first trip. See? And, uh, well, I was, went to work on the boat in her place. So she was able to go back on the boat. Is that on the lake? Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. On the lake. Well, I worked on the boat with Chani. Let me see if I can remember now Chani. Let me see if I can remember. I know Chani. Ruben and Oliver. Ruben was known when I went to, uh, with Sadie and Chani. Huh? No. That's when Ruby taken the boat after Sadie. You know what I'm saying? But Chani, that's when Sadie was living over on Allen Street. No, I didn't know that. Let me see Sadie. Let me see Chani. And they had a little bright fella there. They used to call him Derby. Just about, by a high gun. That's all they ever called him. He was. Derby?
Yeah. He played trumpet or what did he play?
He played, uh, he played sax.

I just remember. Well, that's all right. Buddy P.T. Buddy P.T. was played. Oh, Buddy P.T. played over on the boat? Yeah, Buddy, yeah. On the boat, yeah. That's when it was Buddy. Buddy. That's the gang I played with today. But I didn't know him. I just met him by me coming on a trip down here. And then I stayed here until she got well. She went back on a boat. Then, uh, that's where I met Lawrence Toker. Lawrence. Lawrence come to get her. To get some musician for him to go over to Mandeville or somewhere over that, over the lake to play. You know? And I was, well, I was going to leave that Monday night going back to Birmingham. So by me being over, stayed over. So I stayed over and worked with Lawrence. Them, uh, few nights over the lake, you see. With them. Then I left, went on back to Birmingham to my band, you see.
I want to ask about that band in Birmingham. What was the name of it again?
Uh-huh. I remember some records made by some Birmingham bands. I think one was called Blackbirds of Paradise or something. Do you remember a band like that?
Did you ever make any records over there?
No, I didn't make, no, I never made them. No, I didn't make the record. No, I didn't make the record at all.
Who was the leader of the band? Do you remember? I really don't forgot.
Been a long time, of course.
Been here. Long time. Another thing, I don't like to worry a lot about those old times. I like to hear about it.

I would make it to you. And then, uh, that's the band I played with in Birmingham. All right. I lived in Birmingham. I went down in Florida. I went home, you see. Then, I joined the band of Mac Merrimickles Band. See. I worked with them. See, well, most of all the fellas was in Florida, was out of Florida, except Mac. And also the trombone, he was out of Mobile with George, uh, George Morris. He was out of Mobile. Well, I worked with them. Long time. Just traveling around on the road, see. And then after I, uh, left for Mac Band, I worked with a band in Orlando. A fella named Joe People. That was his name, Joe People.
